questions.q: Which of the following is Cash Management explicitly NOT responsible for?
options: Reconciling bank statements against system transactions
Holding the record of every bank account the business uses
Initiating a payment to a supplier
Giving treasury a short-term cash position
questions.explain: Cash Management consumes payment and receipt transactions created by Payables and Receivables; it does not initiate payments itself.

questions.q: Which work area would you use to load and reconcile a bank statement?
questions.explain: Statement loading, reconciliation, and bank/branch/account setup all live in the Cash Management and Banking work area.

questions.q: In the Bank Account Model, what sits directly between a Bank and a Bank Account?
questions.explain: The hierarchy is Bank → Bank Branch → Bank Account. One bank can have many branches, and one branch can have many accounts.

questions.q: Which work area gives treasury a short-term, account-by-account view used to decide whether to invest or borrow?
questions.explain: Cash Positioning is the short-term, account-level balance view. Cash Forecasting looks further out.

questions.q: Which duty role is required to set up banks, branches, and accounts, typically carried by the Cash Manager job role?
questions.explain: Setup tasks for banks, branches, and accounts require the Cash Management Administration duty role.
